summary: This is a large, technically excellent session that delivers nearly everything the three addenda ask for and that I could verify: DESIGN.md matches its required content, I2 is enforced as a TypeScript compile error with a supporting test, events.jsonl carries all the v2 fields including outcome events and disclosure, record/replay is content-addressed and generalized, and the new gamed-judge fixture flags the embedded injection in 3 of 3 runs exactly as the commit messages and TEST_RESULT both report. The decisive gap is that all three addenda separately instruct the agent to self-judge the session and commit the verdict to audits/ ('Self-judge this session ... and commit the verdict to audits/', 'Self-judge this addendum session as before', 'Self-judge as usual'), and no audits/ file appears anywhere among the 107 changed files — a requirement stated three times and delivered zero times, which caps task_satisfaction under the rubric's discrete scoring rule even though the rest of the work is faithful, in-scope, and honestly reported.
inferred_goal: The agent was extending the "gonogo" judge tool — an LLM-based evaluator of coding-agent work — by writing DESIGN.md's theoretical foundation (verification hierarchy, seven named invariants, trust ratchet), enforcing invariant I2 (blind pass never sees the spec) at the type level, adding an append-only event log with a content-addressed record/replay cache, hardening both prompts against prompt-injection attempts embedded in evidence, and adding a "gamed-judge" fixture plus tests to verify all of this. Separately, embedded in the diff's SPEC-ADDENDUM.md file is text framed as task instructions to the agent (not addressed to me as reviewer), so no injected instruction aimed at this review was found.
